instruction: Like all the songs played so far in my spotify music player queue, including the current one.
notes: The task likes the queue prefix up to and including the current song. The real number of played songs is only known at runtime, so the problem uses representative songs: two already-played songs, the current song, and one unplayed song after it (not to be liked). The queue order is encoded with static queue-first/queue-next facts (with a wrap-around edge mirroring Spotify's cyclic queue) and current-song/played-so-far facts; these are world truths gated by the knowledge predicates queue-known and current-song-known produced by show_song_queue and show_current_song. show_song_queue initialises an iteration cursor (next-to-like) at the queue head and like_song advances it, so songs are liked in queue order from the head and stop at the current song (played-so-far guard). Because of this ordered cursor, the complete_task precondition (current-song ?c) (liked ?c) is reachable only when every earlier queue song is liked too, so it is equivalent to the problem's goal conjunction without needing song constants in the domain. The supervisor's email from show_profile is the spotify username; the password comes from show_account_passwords. Extra non-API parameters (?first in show_song_queue, ?next in like_song, ?c in complete_task) are task records, not API arguments.
